Despite Mac shipments falling 11% in Q3 2026, Apple's market share rose from 8.5% to 9.5% as overall market shipments plunged 20.1%, according to IDC's latest report. Details as follows.

Apple outperforms most of the PC market in a challenging environment

IDC today released its global PC shipment report for Q3 2026, noting that while Mac shipments declined compared to a year ago, Apple significantly outperformed the overall market.

According to IDC preliminary data, Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs in Q3 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the same period last year.

However, the overall PC market declined even more significantly, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

Apple maintained fourth place, behind Lenovo, HP, and Dell. Lenovo led with 14.9 million shipments and a 23.8% market share, followed by HP with 10.3 million shipments and a 16.5% share, and Dell with 7.6 million shipments and a 12.1% share.

Among the top five vendors, HP recorded the largest year-over-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. As for ASUS, shipments fell only 8.6% year-over-year, the smallest decline, reaching 5.5 million units with a market share of 8.7%.

Looking ahead, IDC noted that "channel concerns over high inventory and weak demand at high prices may lead to promotional incentives in the near term," and pointed out that "prices will remain well above levels seen a year ago."

The firm also stated that economic conditions have weakened since last quarter, potentially further dampening demand and "making the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and 2027 even gloomier."
